bottom_line: In ELITE, losartan versus captopril had the same rate of persisting increases in serum creatinine (10.5% in each group; risk reduction 2% [95% CI ⫺51% to +36%], p=0.63).
implications: This 48-week trial in patients aged 65 years or older with symptomatic heart failure and ejection fraction ≤40% shows no difference between losartan and captopril in the prespecified primary renal-dysfunction endpoint (10.5% in each group; risk reduction 2% [95% CI ⫺51% to +36%]). The reported all-cause mortality was lower with losartan than captopril (4.8% vs 8.7%; risk reduction 46% [95% CI 5–69%]), while admissions for heart failure were the same (5.7% in both groups); these findings are limited to this enrolled population and follow-up period as reported.

major_points.text: Prospective double-blind, randomised, parallel, captopril-controlled trial conducted at 125 centres.
major_points.quote: The ELITE study10 was a prospective double-blind, randomised, parallel, captopril-controlled clinical trial conducted at 125 centres in the United States, Europe and South America.

major_points.text: Population: ACE inhibitor naive patients aged 65 years or more with NYHA II–IV heart failure and ejection fraction 40% or less.
major_points.quote: We randomly assigned 722 ACE inhibitor naive patients ( aged 65 years or more) w ith New York Heart Association (NYHA) class II–IV heart failure and ejection fractions of 40% or less

major_points.text: Interventions: losartan titrated to 50 mg once daily versus captopril titrated to 50 mg three times daily, for 48 weeks.
major_points.quote: fractions of 40% or less to double-blind losartan (n=352) titrated to 50 mg once daily or captopril (n=370) titrated to 50 mg three times daily, for 48 w eeks.

major_points.text: Primary endpoint result: persisting increases in serum creatinine occurred at the same frequency in both groups (10.5%).
major_points.quote: There was no significant difference between losartan and captopril in the frequency of the primary endpoint—namely, persisting (confirmed) increases in serum creatinine (10·5% in each group

major_points.text: All-cause mortality was lower with losartan than captopril (4.8% vs 8.7%; risk reduction 46% [95% CI 5–69%], p=0.035).
major_points.quote: This risk reduction w as primarily due to a decrease in all-cause mort alit y ( 4·8% vs 8·7%; risk reduc t ion 46% [ 95% CI 5–69%], p=0·035).

absolute_effects.text: Persisting increase in serum creatinine: 37 (10.5%) with losartan vs 39 (10.5%) with captopril (all patients).
Combined death and/or hospital admission for heart failure: 33 (9.4%) with losartan vs 49 (13.2%) with captopril.
All deaths: 17 (4.8%) with losartan vs 32 (8.7%) with captopril.
Hospital admission for any reason: 78 (22.2%) with losartan vs 110 (29.7%) with captopril.

subgroups.text: Mortality difference was generally consistent across subgroups (age, ejection fraction, aetiology, NYHA class, digoxin use), except deaths in women.
subgroups.quote:
The mortality difference was generally
consistent across different subgroups—namely, age,
ejection fraction, aetiology of heart failure, NYHA
functional class, and concomitant digoxin use, the
exception being deaths in women (9/118 losartan vs 8/122
captopril).

subgroups.text: Creatinine primary endpoint event rates were reported by age subgroup (<70 and ≥70).

harms.text: Discontinuations for adverse effects were less frequent with losartan than captopril (12.2% vs 20.8%).
harms.quote:
Excluding deaths, 43 (12·2%) losartan-treated
patients discontinued for adverse effects versus 77
(20·8%) captopril-treated patients.

harms.text: No losartan-treated patient discontinued due to cough; 14 did in the captopril group.
harms.quote:
14
captopril-treated patients but none of the patients on
losartan discontinued study therapy due to cough.

harms.text: Persisting potassium increases of 0.5 mmol/L or more occurred in 18.8% with losartan and 22.7% with captopril (p=0.069).
harms.quote:
Persisting increases in serum
potassium of 0·5 mmol/L or more above baseline while on
therapy was observed in 66/352 (18·8%) losartan-treated
and 84/370 (22·7%) captopril treated patients (p=0·069).

harms.text: Hypotension-related symptoms occurred overall in 24% of patients; first-dose hypotension was reported in seven captopril and four losartan treated patients.
harms.quote:
There were no differences between the two treatment
groups with respect to hypotension-related symptoms
(occurring overall in 24% of patients). First-dose
hypotension was reported in seven captopril and four
losartan treated patients.

inclusion_criteria.quote: Never received an ACE inhibitor and stable cardiovascular therapy

exclusion_criteria.quote:

analysis_methods.text: Designed with 90% power to detect a 40% reduction in persistent renal dysfunction events, assuming 30% event rate in the captopril group.
analysis_methods.quote:
The study was designed 10 with 90% power to detect a 40%
reduction in persistent renal dysfunction events, assuming a rate
of 30% for such an event in the captopril group.

analysis_methods.text: Creatinine endpoint analysis used a modified intent-to-treat population with endpoints only if both measurements occurred on double-blind therapy.
analysis_methods.quote:
Analysis of increases
in serum creatinine was based upon a modified intent-to-treat
population—ie, all patients were analysed according to their
randomisation group, and an endpoint was declared only if the
initial and confirmatory increases in creatinine occurred while the
patient was on double-blind therapy.

analysis_methods.text: Deaths and heart-failure admissions analyses were intent-to-treat and patients who discontinued were followed to 48 weeks.
analysis_methods.quote:
Analyses of deaths and heart-failure admissions (adjudicated
endpoints) were based on an intent-to-treat population; all
patients who discontinued prematurely were followed up to the
specified 48 weeks.

analysis_methods.text: Time-to-event data analysed with log-rank test.
analysis_methods.quote:
For all time-to-event data, survival analyses were based upon
the log-rank test.

trial_conduct.text: All deaths and hospital admissions were adjudicated by an independent committee blinded to treatment.
trial_conduct.quote: All deaths (including cause of death) and hospital admissions were adjudicated on by an independent Clinical Endpoint Adjudication Committee, blinded to study treatment

criticisms.text: Observed primary-event rate was lower than assumed, reducing power to detect the planned effect size.
criticisms.quote: The event rate proved to be only 10·5% for captopril so the power to detect a 40% reduction was substantially decreased.

criticisms.text: Results cannot be extrapolated beyond elderly patients with systolic dysfunction (eg, younger heart-failure patients or diastolic dysfunction).
criticisms.quote: the results cannot be extrapolated to younger heart-failure patients or patients with diastolic dysfunction.

criticisms.text: Only one-third of enrolled patients were women; mortality in women requires further study.
criticisms.quote: Only one-third of the patients enrolled in ELITE were women, and mortality in women with heart failure taking losartan or captopril requires further study.

criticisms.text: Recruitment was difficult and required a substantial number of sites to reach the sample size.
criticisms.quote: recruitment proved difficult and a substantial number of sites were required to achieve the study sample.
